findings.title: lower() is not case-insensitive for all Unicode: casefold() would be the caseless comparison
findings.body: The docstring promises to "Ignore case", and the code uses Unicode-aware methods (str.isalnum/str.lower), so the function implicitly claims Unicode support. But str.lower() is not a caseless equivalence: Python's casefold() is the method designed for case-insensitive comparison, and lower() misses it for a few characters. Concrete counter-example: the Turkish dotted capital I, U+0130: 'İ'.lower() == 'i\u0307' (i plus a combining dot above), which is not equal to plain 'i', while 'İ'.casefold() == 'i'. As a result is_palindrome("İi") returns False even though, under any case-insensitive reading, both characters are the same letter (casefold gives "ii", a palindrome), whereas is_palindrome("ii") returns True. For ASCII-only input the function is correct; the gap only matters if Unicode text (Turkish, or any script with special case behaviour such as 'ß' vs 'SS') is expected. If Unicode case-insensitivity is in scope, use character.casefold() instead of character.lower(). If the intended input is ASCII, no change is needed and this can be dismissed.
